Examined captured native/ACP close identity; original ACP capability/generation; Keep-working default; full warning/Empty/armed close admission; cover/help/resize invalidation; separate detach; exited-native removal; native/ACP runtime rename without peer/tuple/RPC replacement; and type/name/leaf-path presentation. Examined kind selection; current/independent placement; exact project/profile/settings/option identities; local field rejection and 128-byte launch-name bounds; UTF-8-safe automatic names; original-controller launch FIFO; frozen pending drafts; definite typed rejection with complete inert cause and deliberate retry only; ambiguous transport failure/acknowledged-receipt continuity; and independent-project rollback/isolation without inherited hooks/recipes or directory creation. Followed launch through the real parent, worker, typed client response boundary, daemon reservation and broker startup rather than treating RPC admission as successful initialization.
• e07s05 — Structured project editing and authoritative save preview: 10 assessments, no additional finding. Examined exact selected native/ACP save source; preview/project consistency; fresh canonical cwd/Git-root resolution outside metadata locks; expected_context rejection and source recheck; structured name and nested hook/recipe drafts; ordered hook sources/timeouts; exact recipe names/commands; atomic Apply/persistence/conflict rollback; metadata-only Forget; and mixed-session project-open serialization/reuse. Examined Tab/BackTab focus, mouse/accelerator equivalence, contextual Help/Escape and full error access, canonical attention/outcomes, original controller FIFO and backend capability/generation/RPC admission, force versus explicit interruption, no replay/automatic reacquisition, all ownership mutation panel routes, and owned cleanup/privacy boundaries. findings.title: Ordinary Yield rebases queued gestures onto a newly arrived ownership request
findings.summary: A registered external controller can publish an ordinary manual ownership request while the human's Owner panel is open. draw_panel replaces that panel's claim and observed identity during repaint, but Owner/Yield has no conclusive-input-empty/armed-paint admission. The real parent polls ownership before consuming the next event and explicitly permits ACP repaint while physical input is queued. An old queued y, including a Repeat event, can therefore yield to a requester that did not exist when the gesture was generated. Mouse and focused-button routes also use the repainted current action map rather than claim-bound physical provenance. This is a wrapper consent failure, separate from the deferred native application-buffer settlement limitation. Confidence: 9/10; source-traced execution path, not executed.

locations.role: Owner/Yield submits the repaint-selected claim with the human capability but without presentation readiness
Paint silently replaces displayed claim and observed identity with the latest manual reservation
Mouse admission checks target and panel-kind discriminant, not claim, observation or armed readiness
Ownership action handling accepts Repeat as well as Press
The conclusive-empty callback arms Force only, not ordinary Yield
Ownership updates are polled before repaint and physical-event consumption
ACP screen-null repaint is permitted despite pending input
Valid yield-to revokes the human's original authority and advances the named reservation

evidence.label: Attacker-controlled reservation is rebound into the human's consent sink
evidence.explanation: Owner painting reads the current manual reservation's claim_id and overwrites displayed_claim/displayed_observed. panel_event then accepts y and submits yield-to with that exact newly adopted claim and the genuine human capability. require_source_claim verifies current claim/generation, but cannot establish when the physical gesture was generated.
evidence.excerpt: if displayed_claim.as_deref() != claim { *displayed_claim = claim.map(str::to_owned); } ... if key.code == KeyCode::Char('y') && claim.is_some() { ... "method":"yield-to","claim_id":claim ... }

evidence.label: Actual parent ordering permits old input to cross the identity transition
evidence.explanation: [INFERENCE, source-traced; not executed] Leave the ACP Owner panel open with no manual request, hold the TUI while queuing y, publish a cooperative manual request, allow the ownership projection to become due, then resume. authority.poll observes the request; screen.is_null allows repaint before reading y; draw_panel adopts the claim; y is admitted without Empty or an armed repaint. Alternatively, intervening queued focus events permit consecutive repaints before an old first-button click/Enter, allowing its action map to change from Release to Yield.

evidence.label: Nearby safeguards do not stop this path
evidence.explanation: The stale-observation check compares against the observation just adopted during paint. Mouse checks only the target and discriminant(Owner). The key branch excludes Release, not Repeat. NativeControl::after_draw arms only Force and conditional consent. Backend record_activity preserves ordinary manual reservations, so the preceding original-controller activity RPC does not cancel this request. On ACP's input-admission boundary, a valid yield can offer the reservation to its requester without any native settlement fence.
evidence.excerpt: Event::Key(key) if key.kind != KeyEventKind::Release ... PanelKind::Owner { claim, observed }

evidence.label: Impact is loss of original human authority, not a backend capability bypass
evidence.explanation: The daemon correctly validates the submitted human control and named current reservation, then revokes the human and progresses the request. The defect is that the wrapper creates that authorized mutation from pre-request physical input. The requester can accept its resulting offer; no force or implicit turn interruption is needed.
evidence.excerpt: target.require_source_claim(id, &authority)?; target.revoke(); target.resumable_owner = None; target.mark_yielded(now); target.refresh(now);

findings.remediation: Give ordinary Yield immutable painted provenance containing the target, original grant/generation, observed owner state and exact manual claim_id, plus per-visible-action readiness. Invalidate on arrival/replacement, help/cover, clipping, geometry and authority changes. Require complete successful presentation, conclusive Empty, then an armed repaint before y, focused Enter/Space or mouse can yield; reject Repeat for consent. Keep/return may remain immediate. Preserve backend ownership, retained-work and force/interruption semantics. Add an actual-parent queued-input regression with an external manual request arriving before repaint; assert original human authority remains until a fresh armed exact-claim gesture.

findings.title: Real authentication methods render as indistinguishable blank Authenticate buttons
findings.summary: The genuine broker projects authentication methods as method_id/kind only, but conversation action labels read name exclusively. Missing/null display_value returns an empty string, so every real offered method renders as 'Authenticate: ' without its ID or kind. With multiple agent methods the active action surface cannot distinguish which path is selected; unsupported client/terminal methods look identical too. New synthetic renderer tests supply names that the real broker never emits. Exact-method backend admission remains intact. Confidence: 10/10.
findings.category: should-fix: integrated authentication UX / projection contract

locations.role: Real authentication projection emits method_id and kind, not name
Renderer computes label solely from absent method.name
Every authentication action uses the resulting empty label
Null display values explicitly become empty strings
Synthetic method-choice test supplies names absent from genuine projections

evidence.label: Producer/consumer contract mismatch
evidence.explanation: auth_projection emits only method_id and kind. sync_auth retains those identities but computes method.label from method['name'], which is absent in the real projection. display_value(null) returns an empty string.

evidence.label: The actual activation surface loses distinguishing identity
evidence.explanation: action_label returns 'Authenticate: '+method.label for each method. Details lists IDs, but the focused/clicked action does not identify which method it invokes or its supported kind. The new tests cannot detect the real shape mismatch because their synthetic methods include a name field.

evidence.label: This affects genuine protocol input, not only a synthetic scenario
evidence.explanation: The bundled auth fixture advertises agent-login, client-login and terminal-login. Broker initialization retains their ID/kind pairs, discarding display names, so those genuine methods reach the blank-label consumer. This source review did not execute an authentication flow.

findings.remediation: Use the sanitized exact method_id as the visible fallback when no real label exists, and expose kind/support status in the focused/full action context so methods remain distinguishable. Do not broaden metadata/privacy exposure merely to satisfy synthetic test data. Add a renderer/integration regression using the broker's actual projection shape, with at least two agent methods and an unsupported method; verify F8, Tab/Enter and mouse identify and activate the intended exact method.
